hero_description: The LYNK & CO 900 is a large electrified SUV that drives mainly on its electric motors and calls on a petrol engine for range. EVS services both halves of that system, along with the battery, chassis and assistance electronics.
about_description: The 900 is LYNK & CO's flagship SUV: a three-row model with a plug-in hybrid drivetrain, a substantial battery for electric-only running, air suspension on higher specifications and a full camera and radar assistance suite. Because it can complete most journeys without starting the engine, its servicing needs are unusual — the electric side accumulates the mileage while the engine ages by time, so both schedules matter. EVS treats it as one vehicle with two drivetrains: battery health and thermal testing, inverter and motor diagnostics, engine oil, filter and coolant service, brake and suspension work, software updates and sensor calibration, plus warranty-related repair.

faqs.question: What does servicing the LYNK & CO 900 involve?

faqs.answer: Yes, and on time. Oil degrades by date as well as by distance, and an engine that runs infrequently accumulates moisture and fuel dilution. We service it on the calendar interval rather than waiting for the odometer.
faqs.question: The 900 rarely uses its engine. Does it still need engine servicing?

faqs.answer: Yes. We diagnose and repair compressor, strut and height-sensor faults, then recalibrate the ride-height and assistance systems that depend on the vehicle sitting correctly.
faqs.question: Can you repair the air suspension on the 900?

faqs.answer: Yes. We carry out warranty-related repair and maintenance to manufacturer procedure, documented so your coverage continues without dispute.

name: LiXiang MEGA
hero_title_suffix: Maintenance and EV System Care at EVS
hero_description: The LiXiang MEGA is a fully electric MPV built on a high-voltage architecture for very fast charging. EVS services its battery, charging system, drivetrain and chassis, with warranty-approved procedures throughout.
about_description: The MEGA is LiXiang's fully electric people carrier, and unlike the L-series it has no engine at all. Instead it uses a high-voltage architecture designed for very high charging rates, which makes the charging system, cooling circuits and high-voltage cabling the components that matter most in service. A vehicle designed to add a great deal of range in a few minutes puts real stress on those parts, especially in {{country}} heat, and small faults show up as slower charging long before any warning appears. At EVS we test the battery, charging performance and thermal system, diagnose the drivetrain, service brakes and suspension and carry out warranty-related repair.

faqs.answer: Battery state-of-health and thermal testing, charging system and high-voltage cable inspection, drive unit diagnostics, brake fluid and brake service, tyres and alignment, cabin filter replacement and software verification. There is no engine servicing.
faqs.question: What maintenance does the MEGA need?

faqs.answer: High charging rates generate heat, so the cooling circuit, connectors and cables carry real load. We inspect them and measure charging performance, because a degraded connector or weak coolant flow reduces charging speed before it triggers a fault.
faqs.question: Why does fast charging need specific attention?

faqs.answer: Yes. We test the charge port, high-voltage wiring, onboard systems and battery cooling and compare measured charge rates against expected values to identify the limiting component.
faqs.question: Can you investigate slow charging on the MEGA?

faqs.answer: Yes. We perform warranty-related repair and maintenance to manufacturer procedure and document it so your coverage continues.

hero_description: BMW's i cars share showrooms with petrol models, but underneath they are a different proposition — fifth-generation eDrive motors, no rare-earth magnets, and a battery management strategy of BMW's own. EVS {{country}} services the i4, iX, i5 and i7 with the diagnostics that platform actually needs.
showcase_tagline: BMW i Electric Vehicle Service Centre
about_description: BMW built its electric range on a deliberately conservative idea: keep the car recognisably a BMW and put the innovation in the drivetrain. The fifth-generation eDrive unit combines motor, transmission and power electronics in one housing and uses no rare-earth magnets at all. It is reliable, but when it does need attention it needs the right diagnostic access — and so does the battery management system, which is where most i-series faults are actually read from.

faqs.answer: Yes — i4, iX, i5, i7 and the earlier i3, including battery, drive-unit and charging system work.
faqs.question: Do you service all BMW i models?

faqs.answer: We can. Generic scanners miss most of what a BMW battery management system reports, so we use manufacturer-level diagnostics instead.
faqs.question: Can you read BMW-specific fault codes?

faqs.answer: Yes. Slow charging is usually the onboard charger, the charging port or a thermal limit being applied by the battery management system, and telling those apart takes a proper diagnostic session rather than a guess.
faqs.question: My BMW is slow to charge. Can you diagnose it?

name: Hyundai
hero_title_suffix: EV Service, Maintenance & Repair
hero_description: The Ioniq 5 and Ioniq 6 run on E-GMP, an 800-volt platform that charges faster than almost anything at the price — and asks more of a workshop than most. EVS {{country}} services it properly, including the ICCU and onboard charging faults that generic garages misread.
about_description: Hyundai's E-GMP platform did something unusual: it brought 800-volt charging, vehicle-to-load power output and a genuinely fast charge curve down to a mainstream price. The trade-off is a more complicated electrical architecture. The integrated charging control unit in particular is a known weak point across the Ioniq range, and it presents as a car that will not charge or suddenly loses 12-volt power. Diagnosing it correctly takes brand-level tools, not a code reader.

faqs.answer: Most often the integrated charging control unit. It is a known fault across the Ioniq range and it also shows up as a flat 12-volt battery, so the two get confused. We test both before replacing anything.
faqs.question: My Ioniq 5 will not charge. What is the usual cause?

faqs.answer: It needs different isolation procedures and different test equipment to a 400-volt car. We are set up for it.
faqs.question: Is the Ioniq's 800-volt system harder to service?

faqs.answer: Yes. The Kona uses a 400-volt system rather than E-GMP, and it is covered alongside the Ioniq models at EVS {{city}}.

The GT models add an electronic limited-slip differential and adaptive damping, which are worth knowing about at service time because they need their own diagnostic routines rather than being treated as trim.

faqs.question: Can you service a Kia EV6 GT?
